solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Taken for a ride and abandoned, miles away

indicators.note: away says the letter for miles goes missing from the word before it

parts.note: abandoned means dumped

explanation.surface: Someone was conned and left stranded far from anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes the M out of DUMPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken for a ride is idiom for being cheated or fooled, which is being tricked.

clue.text: Bank customer tied up, stabbed by unusually big Italian

indicators.note: stabbed by says the reversed word is pierced by the scrambled letters
in a down clue up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: roped means tied
OS means outsize, a clothing size for the unusually big

explanation.surface: A customer is tied up and knifed by a hulking Italian in a bank raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a riverbank but it is the financial kind. 'up' works because this is a down clue, so the tied word is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A depositor is someone who pays money into a bank account.

clue.text: Bother to put on duck sauce

indicators.note: in a down clue to put on places the pest above the duck

parts.note: a pest is a bother, a nuisance
a duck is a zero score in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A cook can't be bothered to put sauce on the duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nought, from its egg shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil sauce for pasta.

clue.text: Rests, conserving energy for challenging areas to swim?

indicators.note: conserving means keeping energy within, so it goes inside the word

parts.note: depends, as in rests on, relies on
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A swimmer rests to save energy for the tougher parts of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conserving' puts E inside DEPENDS. The question mark marks a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep ends of pools are where water is deepest, so harder for weak swimmers.

clue.text: Snake tot found stuck in engine

indicators.note: stuck in says the word for tot is lodged inside the engine word

parts.note: a puffer is a child's word for a steam engine or train
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A toddler has a snake stuck in the motor, or the snake is stuck there itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child but is the verb, as in tot up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The puff adder is a venomous African viper, an example of a snake.

clue.text: Young servant, bookish type?

definitions.meaning: a boy attendant, as in a knight's or hotel's
one leaf of a book, playfully a type found in books

explanation.definitionFit: A page is both a boy in service and a sheet in a book.

clue.text: What's supporting e.g. India in turmoil?

definitions.text: What's supporting e.g. India in turmoil?

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: in turmoil says the letters of e.g. India are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: It asks what help is sent to a country like India in crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: aid from abroad supports a country in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign aid is help given by one country to another in need.

clue.text: Name of female lawyer in America, with a husband to support

indicators.note: in a down clue to support puts the lawyer below the other pieces

parts.note: man, as in man and wife
DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A woman's name is wanted for an American lawyer who supports her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Served hideous tripe in diet that is deficient

indicators.note: in puts the mangled word inside what's left of diet
deficient says the diet word lacks those two letters

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

indicators.note: tripe means rubbish, so the word before it is mangled

explanation.surface: Disgusting tripe was dished up as part of a poor diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like the offal dish but works as the anagram signal, meaning rubbish; 'deficient' removes the letters for 'that is', leaving DT around the scrambled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dished out means handed out or distributed, as food is to diners.

clue.text: Chinese societies, heading off for Moroccan hotels

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: triads are Chinese secret criminal societies

explanation.surface: Chinese gangs set off for hotels in Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: A riad is a traditional Moroccan house built round a courtyard, often run as a guesthouse.

clue.text: Old-fashioned rickshaw initially boarded by English traveller

indicators.note: boarded by says the English abbreviation climbs aboard, going inside the other letters

parts.note: passé means out of date, old-fashioned

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of rickshaw

explanation.surface: An English traveller climbs into a quaint old rickshaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The English abbreviation goes inside PASSER, made of the old-fashioned word plus the rickshaw's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone travelling in a vehicle they do not drive.

clue.text: Group of democrats easily confused

indicators.note: group of says a cluster of letters is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A political grouping of democrats is easily bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for being bewildered or lost.

clue.text: Supported United player, perhaps, after attempt to score has fallen short

indicators.note: after puts the player's nickname behind the shortened shot
has fallen short says the word for attempt loses its final letter

parts.note: a shot is an attempt to score a goal
Manchester United players are nicknamed the Reds

explanation.surface: A football report: a United player backs up a team-mate after a shot falls short of goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has fallen short' cuts SHOT to SHO. Manchester United is an English football club whose players are called the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore something up is to prop or support it.

clue.text: Have fewer objections? That's insane

definitions.meaning: read as two words, to ... is to object less
insane here means senseless, without thought

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether objecting less would be madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless means senseless or stupid, close to the loose sense of insane.

clue.text: Several nations meeting up to forge new coalition, ultimately

indicators.note: new says the letters of up to forge are made into something fresh
ultimately takes the final letter of coalition

explanation.surface: Countries convene to build a fresh alliance, eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: The Group of Ten is a forum of industrial countries whose finance ministers confer.

clue.text: In operatic cycle, a French diva starts off very loud?

indicators.note: In says the following pieces go inside the cycle's name

parts.note: Wagner's four-opera cycle is called The Ring
un is French for a

indicators.note: starts off takes the opening letter of diva

explanation.surface: In Wagner's Ring, a French soprano begins very loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts UN and D inside THE RING. The question mark admits that thundering is loud as a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundering describes a deafening noise like thunder, so extremely noisy.

clue.text: Released killer apprehended by relative (daughter)

indicators.note: apprehended by says the killer is held inside the relative

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
an asp is a deadly snake, a killer

explanation.surface: A murderer is caught by a girl's uncle, then let go.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclasped means unfastened, freed from a grip.

clue.text: Watering hole appears empty, animal found

indicators.note: appears here says the bar is seen with the empty letter showing in its middle

parts.note: a watering hole is slang for a pub or bar
O, the figure nought, stands for nothing, empty

explanation.surface: A deserted drinking hole turns up a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig, one kind of animal.

clue.text: Leafy plant rogue left on a ferry

indicators.note: rogue means out of control, so the letters run wild

explanation.surface: A villain abandoned a plant on a ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' looks like a noun for a villain but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal fern is a large fern with broad fronds.

clue.text: Striker fighting to preserve European election coming up

indicators.note: to preserve says the war word holds the next letters within

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up says the poll is read upwards

parts.note: a poll is an election

explanation.surface: A striker fights to keep European elections on the agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer but here simply means someone who hits; 'coming up' reverses because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A walloper is one who hits hard, a heavy hitter.

clue.text: Runs with champion in athletics event

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A champion runner competes at a track meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a contest of speed, the most common kind of track contest.

clue.text: With great joy, William mentioned worker will stop several weeks

indicators.note: will stop says these letters plug the gap within the month

parts.note: July is a month, a span of several weeks

indicators.note: mentioned means the name is spoken, giving only its sound

parts.note: Bill is the short form of William
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A worker called William announces he'll stay several weeks, delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the sound of William's short name is used, so one L is dropped in the spelling; 'will stop' means the pieces plug the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Jubilantly means triumphantly happy, an adverb of rejoicing.

clue.text: Maybe gun points down at gangster, avoiding head and foot

indicators.note: in a down clue down at puts the compass points above the gangster

parts.note: W and E are compass points, west and east

indicators.note: avoiding head and foot drops the top and bottom letters of the gangster's name

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gun is pointed down at a gangster who dodges it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding head and foot' trims CAPONE to APON.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is one example of an arm, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Fellow accompanying queen, working for attendant

indicators.note: accompanying sets the queen's letters alongside the fellow

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A man escorting the queen is working as her attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is a companion who supervises a young person, one kind of attendant.

clue.text: Old crooner engages British group

indicators.note: engages means takes on, so the crooner holds the British letter

parts.note: Perry Como was a mid-century crooner

explanation.surface: A veteran singer hires a British band.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small band of musicians.

clue.text: Blooming learner interrupts start of French test

indicators.note: interrupts says the learner's letter breaks in among the other letters
start of takes the opening letter of French

parts.note: an oral is a spoken test
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner disrupts the beginning of a French oral exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupts' puts L between F and ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral and blooming both describe things full of flowers.

clue.text: Tall, gangly male avoids medicine perhaps

indicators.note: avoids says the male letter is left out

parts.note: a remedy, of which medicine is one kind

explanation.surface: A lanky man refuses his medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy means thin and lanky, like a reed stalk.

clue.text: Regularly train chef to provide food

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Train a chef properly so they can provide meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is a staple grain, eaten as food worldwide.

clue.text: Clean the floor — order rejected by arrogant youngster

indicators.note: by sets the youngster's word beside the reversed order
rejected sends the order's letters back the other way

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
a pup is a cheeky or conceited young man

explanation.surface: A cocky youth refuses an instruction to clean the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to wipe up spilt liquid, cleaning a surface.

clue.text: End part of story still to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the words are spoken, and their sound gives the entry

parts.note: a tale is a story; still as a noun means peace, quiet

explanation.surface: The ending of a story has not yet been heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a final section or appendage added at the end.

clue.text: Military men taking steps to introduce one new regulation

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: to introduce says the steps take in the next letters

parts.note: a dance is a set of steps
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Soldiers take measures to bring in a new rule.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or local law.

clue.text: Line on fabric

parts.note: a ray is a line of light

explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial silk made from cellulose, a textile.
